I've noticed that Legacy of Pander is a fairly highly in-demand card. I
assume its popoularity is based on the idea of having a political deck
with lots of Pander weenies that starts passing vote after vote of LoP
under the user can basically pass any vote he likes. Is this the idea?

If so, how does it work? How do you start getting LoP passed? I would
assume opponents with voting vampires would see this coming and tend
to vote it down, even if it's your Grandpreditor or Grandprey.

Anyone have a deck to post that's worked well for them?

Fred

>

Hmmm. I assume you have to use skill cards to get the presense, seeing as
how there are only 2 Panders with presense. Then what? Bewitching Oration?

>>I would ssume opponents with voting vampires would see this coming

>>and tend to vote it down, even if it's your Grandpreditor or Grandprey.
>
>And? I get out a vampire first turn. Your voting vampire will take 2.
>I pass it unopposed. QED.

Sounds to me like you pretty much want to have an LoP in your opening hand,
particularly if you're towards the end of the line in player order, lest
someone else get a voting vampire out by the second turn. Otherwise, you
might not quite swing the first vote with just the vote card and 2 votes
from Bewitching Oration.

So how many LoPs does it take to have a viable deck?

And how effective is this in comparison to more conventional political
decks?

Fred

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <fred_sXYXY...@netcom.com>, Frederick Scott
<fred_...@netcom.com> writes

>>>If so, how does it work? How do you start getting LoP passed?
>>
>>Speed. Weenies with Presence.
>
>Hmmm. I assume you have to use skill cards to get the presense, seeing as
>how there are only 2 Panders with presense. Then what? Bewitching Oration?
>

Yes, and duplication of the vampires. Also, the little Caitiff with
presence can be useful to pass the vote, though she won't contribute to
its utility. It's very, very possible. Don't forget, all you are going
to need is to pull it off once, quickly, then by the end of your second
turn you have five votes available, most likely (four pander and the one
you use to call a vote). And then call another. And another.

Oh, and don't forget an Info Highway, too.

>>>I would ssume opponents with voting vampires would see this coming
>>>and tend to vote it down, even if it's your Grandpreditor or Grandprey.
>>
>>And? I get out a vampire first turn. Your voting vampire will take 2.
>>I pass it unopposed. QED.
>
>Sounds to me like you pretty much want to have an LoP in your opening hand,

That's kind of the point. If LoP passes FAST, you won't remove it from
the table. They keep throwing more down, and getting more vampires out.

>particularly if you're towards the end of the line in player order, lest
>someone else get a voting vampire out by the second turn.

That's what the BewOra and Awe are for.

> Otherwise, you
>might not quite swing the first vote with just the vote card and 2 votes
>from Bewitching Oration.

This is true. However, you have to watch out for a) drawing votes out
with other votes - a Con Agi, say or b) Cryptic Rider if you *don't*
fail their other votes.

>
>So how many LoPs does it take to have a viable deck?
>

About 7 to 9 seems to be working okay at the moment.

>And how effective is this in comparison to more conventional political
>decks?

Devastatingly so. I've not yet seen it fail to sweep a table, as I
recall.

Don't get me wrong - there *are* holes to be exploited in the deck.
Intercept it has a hard time dealing with, and very, very fast rush (the
three capacity rush decks seen on here) might stand a chance. If you
can secure the ability to vote *down* votes then there is also that
possibility. Contesting the vampires in your deck is possible - keep
working decks round pander vampires, so that you gain lots of votes too.
A weenie Pander bleed deck might be fun. A pander combat deck, with
Unaccpetable Appearance, Jimmy Dunn and Beast and weenie !Nos has been
mentioned. You get votes and kill him, at the same time. A few well-
timed Delaying Tactics will help you, because of the "not this vote
again for the rest of the turn" clause.

However, these holes can be difficult to exploit. Fast rush and
intercept have their own problems, and if sitting cross-table from the
LoP deck, they are going to have to deal with their own predator and
prey first. Many of the other decks end up narrowing your focus overly
so.



Messages.Author: Todd Banister
Messages.Body:
I have been working on a LoP deck now for several months. The absolute key
to the deck is the second round. You must be calling the LoP vote in this
turn before any other voters have a chance. In my 60 card deck there are 17
LoP and one Deal with the devil just in case. I use most of the Panders with
Fredrick the Weak and another low cap Pre Sabbat vamp. Remember, a Pander
does not have to call the vote. Only a Sabbat vampire. This way you can
bring out a Sabbat with Presence on turn one and call the LoP on turn two.
THEN when you bring out the Panders in the following turns the voting now
becomes easy. I have had over 60 table votes with the Pander clan. That is a
blast. Even with the highly tuned deck it still only works about 1/2 the
time due to people burning vote cards, Direct Intervention, intercept,
delaying tactics. All in all a fun deck.

Hope this helps.
Todd Banister
Prince of Atlanta
